independenceStatement: This reviewer did not generate or import these images and did not consult the generating agent's acceptance decisions. Decisions are based on the actual candidate rasters and the current canonical goal texts.
title: Symmetrieeigenschaften verschobener Funktions- und Ableitungsgraphen begründen
description: Die lernende Person kann Symmetrieeigenschaften eines verschobenen Funktionsgraphen oder des Graphen einer Ableitungsfunktion aus Termstruktur, Transformationen oder Ableitungszusammenhängen begründen.
checks: Viewed both actual raster plots and verified the formulas.
f(x)=(x−2)²+1 has symmetry axis x=2, values f(1)=f(3)=2 and vertex (2,1). The left panel correctly demonstrates this.
f′(x)=2(x−2) has values −2,0,2 at x=1,2,3 and is point-symmetric around (2,0); the algebraic identity in the right panel is correct.
defects: The derivative plot labels a point f′(1)=−2, but its vertical dashed projection meets the x-axis distinctly to the right of the x=1 tick. The labelled point and its axis coordinate therefore contradict one another. This is a local tick/projection defect, not an issue with the symmetry formula.
nextAction: Align the x=1 tick with the dashed guide from (1,−2) and keep unit spacing consistent with x=2 and x=3; retain the sound formulas and the existing style.
scope: Targeted independent candidate-image review only. No active-asset import and no full goal-completion or human-approval claim.
